description: Use alongside SDR++/SDR Console during active listening sessions. Shows what's active, what to tune to, and what needs identification. Reads from the spectrum scanner's ClickHouse data.

panels.title: Forensic IQ Captures
panels.description: Raw-IQ capture queue + results from spectrum/iq_capture.py (feature D2). Shows the last 50 forensic_trigger rows across all statuses (pending/captured/blocked/rate_limited/failed). 'captured' rows have a .cs8 path on the host under /var/lib/spectrum/iq_captures — pull it into SDR++/inspectrum. 'blocked' = TETRA/cellular legal blocklist refusal.

targets.rawSql: SELECT   ft.requested_at AS requested_at,   round(ft.freq_hz / 1000000.0, 3) AS freq_mhz,   ft.status AS status,   ft.duration_s AS duration_s,   ft.gain_db AS gain_db,   ft.source AS source,   ft.capture_bytes AS capture_bytes,   ft.capture_path AS capture_path,   ft.error AS error FROM spectrum.forensic_trigger AS ft ORDER BY ft.requested_at DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Tune To These
panels.description: Most interesting frequencies right now, ranked by unusual activity, burstiness, and signal strength. Based on latest full sweep vs 24h history.

targets.rawSql: WITH latest AS (SELECT sweep_id FROM spectrum.sweep_health WHERE preset = 'full' AND dongle_id = '$dongle' ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1), latest_data AS (SELECT round(freq_hz / 100000) * 100000 AS freq_bin, freq_hz, power_dbfs FROM spectrum.scans WHERE dongle_id = '$dongle' AND sweep_id = (SELECT sweep_id FROM latest)), history AS (SELECT round(freq_hz / 100000) * 100000 AS freq_bin, avg(power_dbfs) AS historical_avg, stddevPop(power_dbfs) AS historical_std, countIf(power_dbfs > -40) * 100.0 / count() AS activity_pct FROM spectrum.scans WHERE dongle_id = '$dongle' AND sweep_id LIKE 'full:%' AND timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR GROUP BY freq_bin), kf_lookup AS (SELECT l.freq_hz, max(k.name) AS kf_name, max(k.modulation) AS kf_modulation FROM latest_data l CROSS JOIN spectrum.known_frequencies k WHERE abs(toInt64(l.freq_hz) - toInt64(k.freq_hz)) <= toInt64(greatest(k.bandwidth_hz / 2, 50000)) GROUP BY l.freq_hz) SELECT round(l.freq_hz / 1000000, 3) AS freq_mhz, round(l.power_dbfs, 1) AS current_power, round(h.historical_avg, 1) AS avg_24h, round(l.power_dbfs - h.historical_avg, 1) AS above_normal, round(h.activity_pct, 0) AS activity_pct_24h, CASE WHEN m.kf_name IS NOT NULL THEN m.kf_name WHEN l.freq_hz BETWEEN 118000000 AND 137000000 THEN 'Airband (unidentified)' WHEN l.freq_hz BETWEEN 137000000 AND 156000000 THEN 'VHF Gov/Business' WHEN l.freq_hz BETWEEN 156000000 AND 163000000 THEN 'Marine VHF' WHEN l.freq_hz BETWEEN 163000000 AND 170000000 THEN 'Land Mobile' ELSE 'Unknown' END AS likely_id, CASE WHEN m.kf_modulation IS NOT NULL THEN m.kf_modulation WHEN l.freq_hz BETWEEN 118000000 AND 137000000 THEN 'AM' ELSE 'NFM' END AS mode, CASE WHEN l.power_dbfs - h.historical_avg > 10 THEN 'UNUSUAL' WHEN l.power_dbfs > -15 THEN 'STRONG' WHEN h.activity_pct > 80 THEN 'ALWAYS ON' WHEN h.historical_std > 5 THEN 'BURSTY' ELSE '' END AS status FROM latest_data l JOIN history h ON l.freq_bin = h.freq_bin LEFT JOIN kf_lookup m ON l.freq_hz = m.freq_hz WHERE l.power_dbfs > -40 AND l.freq_hz NOT BETWEEN 174000000 AND 230000000 AND l.freq_hz NOT BETWEEN 88000000 AND 108000000 ORDER BY CASE WHEN l.power_dbfs - h.historical_avg > 10 THEN 0 WHEN h.historical_std > 5 THEN 1 WHEN l.power_dbfs > -15 THEN 2 ELSE 3 END, l.power_dbfs DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Quick Frequency Guide
panels.description: Key Athens frequencies and what mode to use in your SDR software.

targets.rawSql: SELECT name, round(freq_hz / 1000000, 3) AS freq_mhz, modulation AS mode, class_id, notes FROM spectrum.known_frequencies WHERE class_id IN ('am_airband_atc', 'am_airband_atis', 'acars_downlink', 'marine_vhf_channel', 'ais', 'nfm_voice_repeater', 'tetra', 'satcom') ORDER BY multiIf(class_id LIKE 'am_airband%' OR class_id = 'acars_downlink', 1, class_id IN ('marine_vhf_channel', 'ais'), 2, class_id IN ('nfm_voice_repeater', 'tetra'), 3, 4), freq_hz

panels.title: Signal Logger
panels.description: Log what you hear. Submits directly to ClickHouse.

options.content:
# [Open Signal Logger](http://localhost:8084)

Log what you hear during active monitoring sessions.

The form submits directly to ClickHouse — entries appear in the Listening Log panel to the right.

**Tip:** You can also bookmark the logger page or keep it in a separate tab.

panels.title: Listening Log
panels.description: Recent signal identifications from monitoring sessions.

targets.rawSql: SELECT timestamp, freq_mhz, mode, class_id, heard, language, notes FROM spectrum.listening_log ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Last Hour — Signal Activity
panels.description: Max power per minute for key signal groups. Shows what's been happening while you set up.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toStartOfInterval(timestamp, INTERVAL 1 MINUTE) AS time, maxIf(power_dbfs, freq_hz BETWEEN 118000000 AND 122000000) AS ATC, maxIf(power_dbfs, freq_hz BETWEEN 146000000 AND 153000000) AS Military_VHF, maxIf(power_dbfs, freq_hz BETWEEN 156000000 AND 163000000) AS Marine, maxIf(power_dbfs, freq_hz BETWEEN 164000000 AND 170000000) AS Land_Mobile FROM spectrum.scans WHERE dongle_id = '$dongle' AND (sweep_id LIKE 'airband:%' OR sweep_id LIKE 'full:%') AND timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

panels.title: Burst Radar — Last 30 min
panels.description: Signals that just spiked — active voice traffic, dispatch, or new transmissions. These are the most interesting things to tune to.

targets.rawSql: WITH kf_lookup AS (SELECT DISTINCT e.freq_hz, max(k.name) AS kf_name FROM spectrum.events e CROSS JOIN spectrum.known_frequencies k WHERE abs(toInt64(e.freq_hz) - toInt64(k.freq_hz)) <= toInt64(greatest(k.bandwidth_hz / 2, 50000)) AND e.event_type = 'appeared' AND e.timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 30 MINUTE GROUP BY e.freq_hz) SELECT e.timestamp, round(e.freq_hz / 1000000, 2) AS freq_mhz, round(e.power_dbfs, 1) AS power, round(e.prev_power, 1) AS was, round(e.delta_db, 1) AS jump_db, ifNull(m.kf_name, 'Unknown') AS signal_name, CASE WHEN e.freq_hz BETWEEN 118000000 AND 137000000 THEN 'AM' ELSE 'NFM' END AS tune_mode FROM spectrum.events e LEFT JOIN kf_lookup m ON e.freq_hz = m.freq_hz WHERE e.event_type = 'appeared' AND e.timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 30 MINUTE ORDER BY e.timestamp DESC LIMIT 15

panels.title: Airband Status
panels.description: Current airband conditions: ATIS presence and ATC burst activity.

targets.rawSql: SELECT 'ATIS' AS signal, ifNull(round(max(power_dbfs), 1), -99) AS current_power, CASE WHEN max(power_dbfs) > -48 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'QUIET' END AS status FROM spectrum.scans WHERE dongle_id = '$dongle' AND freq_hz BETWEEN 136000000 AND 136300000 AND (sweep_id LIKE 'airband:%' OR sweep_id LIKE 'full:%') AND timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE UNION ALL SELECT 'ATC Bursts (15m)' AS signal, toFloat64(count()) AS current_power, CASE WHEN count() > 5 THEN 'BUSY' WHEN count() > 0 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'QUIET' END AS status FROM spectrum.events WHERE dongle_id = '$dongle' AND freq_hz BETWEEN 118000000 AND 137000000 AND event_type = 'appeared' AND timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE

panels.title: Marine Status
panels.description: Current marine band conditions: Ch16, AIS, and marine burst activity.

targets.rawSql: SELECT 'Ch16 Distress' AS signal, ifNull(round(max(power_dbfs), 1), -99) AS current_power, CASE WHEN max(power_dbfs) > -48 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'QUIET' END AS status FROM spectrum.scans WHERE dongle_id = '$dongle' AND freq_hz BETWEEN 156700000 AND 156900000 AND sweep_id LIKE 'full:%' AND timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE UNION ALL SELECT 'Marine Bursts (15m)' AS signal, toFloat64(count()) AS current_power, CASE WHEN count() > 5 THEN 'BUSY' WHEN count() > 0 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'QUIET' END AS status FROM spectrum.events WHERE dongle_id = '$dongle' AND freq_hz BETWEEN 156000000 AND 163000000 AND event_type = 'appeared' AND timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE UNION ALL SELECT 'AIS' AS signal, ifNull(round(max(power_dbfs), 1), -99) AS current_power, CASE WHEN max(power_dbfs) > -45 THEN 'ACTIVE' ELSE 'QUIET' END AS status FROM spectrum.scans WHERE dongle_id = '$dongle' AND freq_hz BETWEEN 161900000 AND 162100000 AND sweep_id LIKE 'full:%' AND timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 15 MINUTE

panels.title: Mystery Signals
panels.description: Strong unidentified signals (> -30 dBFS) not in the known_frequencies table. Tune in and identify!

targets.rawSql: WITH latest AS (SELECT sweep_id FROM spectrum.sweep_health WHERE preset = 'full' AND dongle_id = '$dongle' ORDER BY timestamp DESC LIMIT 1), kf_match AS (SELECT DISTINCT s.freq_hz FROM spectrum.scans s CROSS JOIN spectrum.known_frequencies k WHERE s.dongle_id = '$dongle' AND s.sweep_id = (SELECT sweep_id FROM latest) AND abs(toInt64(s.freq_hz) - toInt64(k.freq_hz)) <= toInt64(greatest(k.bandwidth_hz / 2, 50000))) SELECT round(s.freq_hz / 1000000, 2) AS freq_mhz, round(s.power_dbfs, 1) AS power, 'NFM' AS try_mode FROM spectrum.scans s WHERE s.dongle_id = '$dongle' AND s.sweep_id = (SELECT sweep_id FROM latest) AND s.freq_hz NOT IN (SELECT freq_hz FROM kf_match) AND s.power_dbfs > -30 AND s.freq_hz NOT BETWEEN 174000000 AND 230000000 AND s.freq_hz NOT BETWEEN 88000000 AND 108000000 ORDER BY s.power_dbfs DESC LIMIT 10

panels.title: Unknowns Ranked by Interest
panels.description: Peaks that classified as unknown or with low confidence, sorted by activity. Pick from the top and use the Signal Logger to confirm.

targets.rawSql: SELECT   round(pf.freq_hz / 1000000.0, 3) AS freq_mhz,   sc.class_id AS current_class,   sc.confidence AS confidence,   round(pf.duty_cycle_24h, 3) AS duty_24h,   pf.bandwidth_hz AS bandwidth_hz,   round(pf.power_mean_dbfs, 1) AS power_mean_dbfs,   pf.sweeps_observed_24h AS sweeps_observed FROM (SELECT freq_hz, duty_cycle_24h, bandwidth_hz, power_mean_dbfs, sweeps_observed_24h       FROM spectrum.peak_features FINAL) AS pf LEFT JOIN (SELECT freq_hz, class_id, confidence FROM spectrum.signal_classifications FINAL) AS sc   ON sc.freq_hz = pf.freq_hz WHERE pf.sweeps_observed_24h > 5   AND (sc.class_id LIKE 'unknown_%' OR sc.confidence < 0.5) ORDER BY duty_24h DESC LIMIT 20

panels.title: Blind Signal Features
panels.description: Modulation identity cards from spectrum/analysis/blind_analyze.py (feature D3). Each row is one .cs8 capture analyzed blind: modulation family, occupied bandwidth, carrier offset, baud, and OFDM flag. 'digital-unknown' = encrypted/unrecognized, labeled out-of-scope, never decoded. baud/OFDM cells are blank when the estimate did not clear its confidence bar.

targets.rawSql: SELECT   analyzed_at,   round(freq_hz / 1000000.0, 3) AS freq_mhz,   modulation,   round(confidence, 2) AS confidence,   round(occupied_bw_hz / 1000.0, 1) AS occupied_bw_khz,   round(carrier_offset_hz / 1000.0, 2) AS carrier_offset_khz,   baud_hz,   baud_confidence,   ofdm_flag,   ofdm_tu_us,   round(snr_db, 1) AS snr_db,   source FROM spectrum.blind_signal_features ORDER BY analyzed_at DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Signal of the Day
panels.description: One pick per day from spectrum/anomalies.py, newest first, with the written reason. The interest score favors unnamed, new and rare emitters and pushes broadcast FM, DVB-T and artifact suspects to the bottom. Re-picked every hour, sent in the 21:00 digest.

targets.rawSql: SELECT toString(day) AS day, round(center_hz / 1000000.0, 3) AS freq_mhz, name, name_source AS named_by, dongle_id, score, reason FROM spectrum.signal_of_the_day FINAL ORDER BY day DESC LIMIT 7

panels.title: Active Emitters
panels.description: Emitters on the selected dongle with a peak in the last hour (spectrum.emitters_current, rebuilt every 15 min). An emitter is one transmitter: adjacent bins that peak across many sweeps. Unnamed and new first, broadcast and artifact suspects last, roughly the order of rf.py now, which has the exact score. ARTIFACT SUSPECT rows are the receiver's own spurs, not transmitters.

targets.rawSql: SELECT round(center_hz / 1000000.0, 3) AS freq_mhz, name, name_source AS named_by, if(artifact_suspect, concat('ARTIFACT SUSPECT: ', artifact_reason), if(tetra_network != '', concat('TETRA ', tetra_network, if(tetra_mode = 'continuous', ', likely control channel', ', bursty')), '')) AS flag, round(100 * duty_overall, 1) AS duty_pct, hours_observed, first_seen, last_seen, emitter_id FROM spectrum.emitters_current WHERE dongle_id = '$dongle' AND last_seen > now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR ORDER BY artifact_suspect, class_id IN ('broadcast_fm', 'dvbt_mux') OR service IN ('broadcast_fm', 'dvb_t_gr'), name_source NOT IN ('allocation', 'signal_catalog', 'unnamed'), first_seen DESC LIMIT 50

panels.title: Today's Anomalies
panels.description: What was new or strange in the last 24 h, both dongles (spectrum.anomalies, hourly). Kinds: new_emitter, gone_quiet, louder_than_usual, broken_pattern, new_tetra_carrier. Silence counts swept hours only, so a session gap is never gone_quiet. confidence low = a level anomaly from a dongle whose levels are not trusted (the water-damaged V4).

targets.rawSql: SELECT event_at, kind, round(center_hz / 1000000.0, 3) AS freq_mhz, name, dongle_id, confidence, detail FROM spectrum.anomalies FINAL WHERE event_at > now() - INTERVAL 24 HOUR ORDER BY confidence = 'low', event_at DESC LIMIT 100

panels.title: TETRA Networks
panels.description: TETRA carriers per network on the primary dongle (dongle_roles, the V3). public_safety is 380-400 MHz, civil 410-430 MHz, other is anywhere else and is a finding. A continuous carrier is likely a base station's control channel. Tile-grid spurs with a tetra label are left out. Occupancy from sweep data only: nothing is captured or decoded.

targets.rawSql: SELECT network, carriers, likely_control_channels, bursty, outside_known_allocation, also_on_secondary, secondary_only, hours_observed FROM spectrum.tetra_networks ORDER BY network = 'other', network

panels.title: TETRA Activity by Hour of Day
panels.description: Per network, the share of covering sweeps with a peak on its carriers, by hour of day in Athens time, primary dongle only. Hours the dongle never swept stay blank, they are not 0 %. A swept hour with no peak is dark.

targets.rawSql: SELECT hour_of_day, 100 * maxIf(duty, network = 'public_safety') AS `public safety`, 100 * maxIf(duty, network = 'civil') AS `civil`, 100 * maxIf(duty, network = 'other') AS `other` FROM spectrum.tetra_network_hourly GROUP BY hour_of_day ORDER BY hour_of_day

panels.title: TETRA Carriers
panels.description: Every TETRA carrier per dongle. The primary (V3) is the source of truth. Secondary rows show what the V4 also sees, never its levels. mode: continuous (likely control channel) or bursty, from the duty cycle. finding marks a carrier outside every known TETRA allocation.

targets.rawSql: SELECT network, role, dongle_id, center_mhz, mode, round(100 * duty_overall, 1) AS duty_pct, hours_observed, if(outside_known_allocation, 'outside every known TETRA allocation', '') AS finding, other_dongle_sees_it AS on_other_dongle, evidence, name, last_seen FROM spectrum.tetra_carriers ORDER BY network, role, center_mhz

panels.title: Occupancy Atlas
panels.description: M1: per band and hour, the share of sweeps in which the peak detector fired, averaged over the band's 1 MHz cells (spectrum.occupancy_hourly). Only swept time counts: hours the dongle was unplugged are blank, and a swept band with no peak is dark, 0 %. Raw peaks, so tile-grid spurs and FM intermodulation add some false occupancy.

targets.rawSql: SELECT hour AS time, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 88 AND 107) AS `FM broadcast 88-108`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 108 AND 117) AS `aero nav 108-118`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 118 AND 136) AS `airband 118-137`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 137 AND 143) AS `weather sats 137-144`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 144 AND 145) AS `2 m ham 144-146`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 146 AND 155) AS `gov, business 146-156`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 156 AND 161) AS `marine 156-162`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 162 AND 173) AS `land mobile 162-174`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 174 AND 229) AS `DVB-T 174-230`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 230 AND 379) AS `military aero 230-380`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 380 AND 399) AS `TETRA public safety 380-400`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 400 AND 409) AS `unallocated 400-410`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 410 AND 429) AS `TETRA civil 410-430`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 430 AND 445) AS `70 cm, ISM 430-446`, avgIfOrNull(active_pct, band_mhz BETWEEN 446 AND 469) AS `PMR446, land mobile 446-470` FROM spectrum.occupancy_hourly WHERE dongle_id = '$dongle' AND $__timeFilter(hour) GROUP BY time ORDER BY time

list.name: dongle
list.label: Dongle
list.query: SELECT dongle_id FROM spectrum.sweep_health WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY GROUP BY dongle_id ORDER BY dongle_id
list.definition: SELECT dongle_id FROM spectrum.sweep_health WHERE timestamp > now() - INTERVAL 30 DAY GROUP BY dongle_id ORDER BY dongle_id
list.description: Which RTL-SDR dongle to read. The list comes from dongles that scanned in the last 30 days. The default is the official scanner dongle (v3-01 since 2026-09-26); change current.value here when that changes.

title: Listening Playbook
